speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To help me understand your condition better, how long have you had these symptoms, and can you describe the appearance and location of the skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota, the left knee pain a week ago, and now this wrist pain with fever, I suspect a tick-borne infection like Lyme disease. Have you noticed any tick bites or a rash on your body, and do you recall a "bull's-eye" rash anywhere?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Multiforme Major (likely triggered by a recent viral infection such as Parvovirus B19 or Mycoplasma pneumoniae, given the violaceous targetoid lesions on acral surfaces and preceding joint pain). The "Minnesota camping" and tick history were likely red herrings for a viral etiology.
